newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mixed in early trading.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mixed in early trading.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed in early trading, digesting developments concerning European economic and monetary union (EMU).
June mark futures were higher but off from their overnight highs, but June Swiss were lower.
Traders pondered news that German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition agreed on Tuesday to back down from its controversial plan to revalue central bank assets.
Traders also noted unsubstantiated talk of a one-year delay in EMU.
"There's really a lot to digest," one IMM analyst said.
The Socialist win in the French election this weekend and concerns about a rift between Bonn and the Bundesbank over German asset revaluation had fueled dollar gains on Monday.
June marks and Swiss challenged support levels on Monday, but marks edged up from those losses on Tuesday.
The IMM analyst said the idea that the Bonn-Bundesbank rift had been resolved took some pressure off marks.
But overall, he said IMM markets were quiet, with cash cross action -- not the dollar -- dominating.
"It's a quiet market and I think the dollar markets will be quiet ahead of Friday's job report," the analyst said.
Traders agreed, saying trade may turn lackluster heading into the Friday data.
U.S. May jobs were forecast to rise 221,000 compared with 142,000 in the previous report. The jobless rate was forecast at 5.0 percent, up from 4.9 percent in April.
For the time being, traders said currency futures action would be dominated by mark futures as EMU talk takes center stage.
One broker said he was surprised that Canadian dollar futures were so quiet. He said only 1,200 contracts had traded in the first 45 minutes.
Canadian dollar futures fell overnight but opened near unchanged after final results in Canada's general election showed that the ruling Liberal party won by a narrow margin.
June Canadian dollar sank to $0.7235 overnight but recovered to reach $0.7296 in day session trade. Overall, June Canadian dollar was tethered to Monday's closing level.

At 0839 CDT/1339 GMT, yen was up $0.000035 at $0.008626, marks rose $0.0009 to $0.5792, Swiss franc eased $0.0031 to $0.6962, sterling rose $0.0020 to $1.6362, Can dollar rose $0.0002 to $0.7280, Aussie dollar lost $0.0001 to $0.7580, Mexican peso lost $0.000025 to $0.125600.
